title: Cross-region watermarking and synthetic-replay validator for retrospective usage reconciliation
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background: Console per-model charts and tenant heatmaps have sporadic drift when late/backfilled events arrive from other regions or from replayed historical ingestion jobs. Current mitigations (naive dedupe and shard-watermarks) reduce some noise but do not prevent multi-region ordering-induced double-counts or attribution jitter when model aliases change. This ticket implements a cross-region watermarking scheme and an automated synthetic-replay validator to detect, quantify, and flag retrospective reconciliation divergence before customer-visible console updates are applied.

Goals: (1) ensure reconstructed per-model and per-route usage metrics remain stable after retrospective/late ingest and cross-region replays, (2) detect reconciliation divergence early and produce actionable corrective runs or backfill tickets, (3) provide dashboards and alerts that signal when automated fixes are safe to apply versus when manual investigation is required.
design_notes: Introduce region-level monotonically-increasing ingest watermarks based on event logical time + source offset; watermarks stored in durable metastore with causal ties to shard checkpoints.

Attach idempotency token + ordinal (event_seq) at ingestion boundary so replayed events can be collapsed deterministically. Canonicalize event source name mapping to handle model aliasing during reconciliation.
Add a reconciliation scorer that compares 'live' aggregates vs 'reconstructed' aggregates over a rolling 24/72/168-hour window and emits divergence vectors per tenant/model/route.

Build a synthetic-replay job generator: it will produce deterministic synthetic traffic (prefix distributions, model mix, small/med/large token sizes) and feed it into a shadow ingestion pipeline to validate end-to-end accounting correctness after watermark/backfill logic changes.
Expose a reconciliation summary API consumed by Console: percent-delta, absolute-token-delta, top-k model contributors to drift, and confidence score for automated correction eligibility.
Define safe-apply policy: automated correction auto-runs only if per-tenant percent-delta < 0.5% and top model contributors cover > 90% of delta and synthetic-replay agreements are within thresholds.
Fallback: when thresholds breached, surface an investigation ticket with replay artifacts and shard-level diffs; do not mutate customer-facing aggregates.
Data retention: keep raw reconciliation diffs for 90 days to support audits and customer inquiries.
implementation_steps: Schema change: add 'ingest_ordinal' and 'idempotency_key' to the transport envelope; implement backwards-compatible parsing for older producers.
Metastore: deploy region_watermarks table with per-shard checkpoint + last_seen_logical_time; lightweight TTL-based GC for stalled shards.
Ingest path: compute region watermark at write time (logical_time + region_offset) and attach to events; update watermark on successful commit.
Reconstruction pipeline: enhance aggregator to use ingest_ordinal and idempotency_key to collapse duplicates deterministically during backfill processing.
Scorer service: implement reconciliation comparator that runs nightly and on-demand synthetic replays; generate per-tenant/model divergence vectors and store summary metrics.

Synthetic-replay harness: build deterministic workload generator (three templates: small dev tenant, midgrowth, enterprise surge) and a harness to feed shadow cluster(s) with controllable clock skew and region-routing.
Console integration: add reconciliation panel and an alerting widget that surfaces when automated correction is disabled for a tenant due to divergence.
Automation: implement safe-apply orchestration that performs dry-run corrections, validates via a fast synthetic replay, and then applies corrections under the safe-apply policy.
Testing & canary: deploy in canary region, run 72h stress synthetic replays; compare metrics; iterate on thresholds.
Docs & runbook: produce a runbook for oncall with triage steps, invariant checks, and links to replay artifacts and shard logs.
PRs & rollout: open stacked PRs for schema, ingest, metastore, and scorer service; coordinate migration window for producers to adopt idempotency envelope.
acceptance_criteria: Reconstruction and live aggregates for synthetic replay inputs match within 0.25% token delta across 3 workload templates after canary run.
Nightly reconciliation job runs without >1% false-positive divergence alerts across a 48-hour test fleet (synthetic + shadow real tenants).
Console reconciliation panel shows top-5 contributing models to any divergence with links to replay artifacts.
Automated safe-apply corrections execute successfully in canary and include dry-run validation step present in logs and audit trail.
No customer-facing billing changes occur in canary tenants without manual signoff when divergence >0.5%.
Migration of producers to attach idempotency_key is backward compatible and does not cause ingestion errors during the rollout window.
Runbook created and reviewed by reliability and billing teams; oncall can complete triage checklist within documented 30 minutes.
monitoring_and_metrics: dashboards: reconciliation overview, per-model drift waterfall, region watermark heatmap
testing_plan: Unit tests for envelope parsing and idempotency collapse logic.
Integration tests with local shadow ingest pipeline processing synthetic workloads.
Regression test: replay historical backlog snapshot and verify dedupe + attribution correctness against golden sample.
Canary test: enable in us-west-2 with 50 synthetic tenants for 72 hours and run daily reconciliation; log discrepancies and iterate.
Chaos test: introduce controlled out-of-order delivery and clock skew during synthetic replays to validate watermark robustness.
Load test: run synthetic enterprise template to exercise shard merge and backfill paths and ensure scorer latency < 60s for nightly job.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Dev): implement schema + scorer + synthetic harness; internal integration testing.
Phase 2 (Canary region): enable ingest watermarking for shadow path only; run synthetic replays and compare; adjust thresholds.
Phase 3 (Selective tenants): opt-in enterprise tenants for dry-run corrections and provide billing-safe reports to customers for verification.
Phase 4 (Global): flip safe-apply in regions that passed canary; monitor for 7 days before broad enablement.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Aisha Raman: initial spike showed idempotency collapse reduces duplicate counts by ~70% in local replay. Need to discuss ordinal generation with infra team.
2026-03-01 - Carlos Vega: prototyped region_watermarks table and it attaches with <1ms overhead; pushing schema PR next.
2026-03-08 - Maya Patel (Billing): confirm we should never auto-correct billing-affecting aggregates without manual approval; propose dry-run reports to customers when corrections are applied.
2026-03-10 - Reliability: added chaos test for 8s clock skew; early failure modes indicate we must increase TTL on shard checkpoints to handle delayed commit windows.
